results.title: How subscriptions work
results.content:
### Previous successfully paid invoices

The page **does not explicitly say** whether a `past_due` or `unpaid` subscription can have earlier successfully paid invoices. It defines those statuses by reference to the invoice or invoices currently governing the subscription’s status—not as a record of the subscription’s entire payment history.

Relevant wording:

> **`past_due`:** “Payment on the latest finalized invoice either failed or wasn’t attempted. When status resolution uses all invoices, `past_due` can also indicate that an earlier applicable invoice remains outstanding.”

> **`unpaid`:** “The invoice or invoices governing subscription status haven’t been settled, but the subscription remains in place.”

> “When you use all invoices for status resolution: … An `unpaid` subscription remains `unpaid` until you settle applicable outstanding invoices.”

The page also says:

> “The subscription continues to generate invoices but doesn’t attempt payment. Revoke access to your product when the subscription is `unpaid` because Stripe already attempted and retried payment while the subscription was `past_due`.”

So, the status definitions identify failed, unattempted, or unsettled invoice(s), but **the page does not explicitly confirm whether earlier invoices were successfully paid**.

### Does status alone prove the subscription was never billed?

**No.** The page does not say that `past_due` or `unpaid` means the subscription was never billed. It says unpaid subscriptions continue generating invoices, and that payment was already attempted and retried while the subscription was `past_due`.

For contrast, the page specifically describes `incomplete_expired` this way:

> “The initial payment on the subscription failed and the customer didn’t make a successful payment within 23 hours of subscription creation. These subscriptions don’t bill customers.”

That statement applies to `incomplete_expired`; it does not establish that other statuses prove a subscription was never billed.

### Trial-end conversion, including early trial end

The page says:

> “If you create a trial period to delay the first charge for the subscription, the initial status is `trialing`, and the subscription automatically transitions to `active` when the trial ends and payment succeeds.”

It also says:

> **`trialing`:** “The subscription is currently in a trial period and you can safely provision your product for your customer. The subscription transitions automatically to `active` when a customer makes the first payment.”

The page **does not describe an early-trial-end procedure** or explicitly say how conversion works when a trial ends before its scheduled end.

results.title: Subscriptions | Stripe API Reference
results.content:
- The page does not state whether `past_due` or `unpaid` subscriptions can have previously paid invoices.
- The page does not state whether a subscription’s status alone proves it has never been billed.
- The page does not describe conversion when a trial ends early.
- Relevant wording on the page: “Subscriptions allow you to charge a customer on a recurring basis.”
